body.statement: For every finite revealed graph \(G\), an exact branch-safe compiler first evaluates whether \(M_n<n\). If \(M_n\ge n\), it forms none of \(\pi_i(G)\), \(Q_G\), \(w_i(z;G)\), or \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{seed}}\), and returns the all-treated estimator with worst-case MSE at most \(1=\overline U(G)\). If \(M_n<n\), it enumerates the \(n^{k_n}\) ordered seed tuples, groups them by \(Z^{\mathrm{seed}}\), computes every positive \(\pi_i(G)\), every \(w_i(z;G)\), \(Q_G\), and a certified enclosure of \(\lambda_{\max}(Q_G)\), and returns the seed estimator when \(U(G,k_n)\le1\) or the all-treated fallback otherwise, with worst-case MSE at most \(\overline U(G)\). On the high-probability certificate event in Open-ended Question 1, \(\overline U(G_n)\le C_Ur(n,d_n)\).
body.justification: The matched statistical frontier comes with an exact finite procedure that never evaluates an inverse exposure probability outside its positive-probability branch.
body.gap: KandirosHarshawSavje2026Minimax, Algorithm 4 with Proposition 4.3, gives a polynomial approximation design for its conflict-graph criterion using the imported Partial Vertex Cover 2-approximation in Theorem C.11; it does not provide this branch-safe exact seed-law certificate or close the random-regular GATE minimax gap.
body.consumer: An experimenter can audit the assignment law and worst-case error on the actual revealed network before running the one-shot study.
body.proof_tex:
The branch test uses only the revealed graph and the deterministic number \(M_n=d_n^2+1\).  If \(M_n\ge n\), Definition~\(\mathrm{def{:}certified\mbox{-}procedure}\) forms no inverse probability.  Its all-treated report is \(\mu_1\), so its error for \(\tau_n=\mu_1-\mu_0\) equals \(\mu_0\).  By Cauchy--Schwarz and the control endpoint restriction,
\[
\mu_0^2=\left(\frac1n\sum_i b_i\right)^2\le\frac1n\sum_i b_i^2\le1=\overline U(G).
\tag{19}
\]
This includes the smallest admissible regular instance \((n,d_n)=(4,3)\), so the branch rule never divides by a zero exposure probability there.

Suppose \(M_n<n\).  Then \(m_i(G)\le M_n\) gives \(q_i(G)\ge1-M_n/n>0\), and hence every \(\pi_i(G)=q_i(G)^{k_n}\) is positive.  There are exactly \(n^{k_n}\) ordered seed tuples.  Enumerating them, mapping each to its union assignment, and grouping equal assignments computes the seed-design mass of every supported \(z\) and the finite conditional averages \(w_i(z;G)\).  The same graph computation supplies \(m_i\) and \(h_{ij}\), hence all entries of \(K_G\) and \(Q_G\).  These entries are rational.  The largest eigenvalue of the rational symmetric matrix \(Q_G\), and the operator norm entering \(U(G,k_n)\), admit certified rational enclosures by bisection together with exact positive-semidefiniteness tests for the corresponding shifted rational matrices.  Thus every comparison used by the compiler is a finite graph computation.

If \(U(G,k_n)\le1\), Lemma~\(\mathrm{lem{:}schur\mbox{-}certificate}\) bounds the worst-case MSE of the returned seed estimator by \(U(G,k_n)=\overline U(G)\).  If \(U(G,k_n)>1\), the compiler returns the all-treated estimator, and (19) bounds its MSE by \(1=\overline U(G)\).  Therefore the compiler is branch-safe and always has worst-case MSE at most \(\overline U(G)\).  Finally, on the event specified in Open-ended Question~\(\mathrm{oeq{:}boolean\mbox{-}operator}\), namely \(U(G_n,k_n)\le C_Ur(n,d_n)\),
\[
\overline U(G_n)\le\min\{1,U(G_n,k_n)\}\le C_Ur(n,d_n),
\]
which proves the last conditional assertion without presuming that the event has high probability.
